cards.title: 3.1.1 Carbohydrates
body: Carbohydrates are the most abundant organic compounds in living organisms.
Based on the sugar units they contain, carbohydrates are classified as monosaccharides, disaccharides or polysaccharides.
Carbohydrates are mainly found in plants such as potatoes, rice and wheat.
Monosaccharides are single sugar containing molecules.

cards.title: 3.1.2 Lipids
body: The word lipid comes from the Greek word “lipos”, meaning “fat” or “lard” (fat of pork/a pig).
Like carbohydrates, lipids are large molecules made up of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.
The most common lipids are fats, oils and waxes.
Lipids are found in animals and plants e.g. butter and groundnut oil.

cards.title: 3.1.3 Proteins
body: Protein molecules are made up of long chains of smaller molecules joined end to end.
Amino acids are classified as essential or non-essential amino acids.
Essential amino acids are those which cannot be synthesized by the body.
Non-essential amino acids are those that the body can synthesize from other amino acids or nutrients present in food.

cards.title: 3.1.4 Nucleic acids
body: The two nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) vary in some of their structural components and in their functions.
Deoxyribonucleic acid contains deoxyribose and ribonucleic acid contains ribose.
Deoxyribonucleic acid is a long molecule made up of two strands of materials, which are twisted into a shape called a double helix.
The double helix looks like a ladder that has been twisted into a spiral staircase.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following carbohydrates is used as the primary storage molecule for excess glucose in animal liver and muscle cells?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Check storage forms of glucose**
*   Plants store excess glucose as starch.
*   Animals store excess glucose as glycogen, mainly inside the liver and skeletal muscle cells.
*   Cellulose forms plant cell walls.
*   Chitin forms fungal cell walls.

**Final Result:**
**Glycogen** is the correct answer.

**Proteins**.

lessons.title: The Energy Flow in Photosynthesis and Cellular Respiration

cards.title: 3.2 The Energy Flow in Photosynthesis and Cellular Respiration
body: Photosynthesis is a chemical process that takes place in plants to make food.
Green plants use solar energy to make biomolecules.
Most plants have a green substance, called chlorophyll, found inside the chloroplasts of plant cells.
Plants get carbon dioxide from the air, whereas water is absorbed from the soil by their root hairs.
Photosynthesis occurs in two reactions, called a light reaction and a dark reaction.

cards.title: Formula
body: Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂
Light + chlorophyll. Respiration is the reverse energy story: glucose broken to release ATP.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: During heavy and intense exercise, human muscle cells may run out of oxygen and switch to anaerobic respiration. What organic byproduct is formed in this reaction?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Check human anaerobic respiration products**
*   In human muscle cells under oxygen deficit, glucose is partially broken down via lactic acid fermentation.
*   This process produces lactic acid and $$2\text{ ATP}$$.
*   Ethanol and carbon dioxide are byproducts in yeast fermentation, not human muscles.

**Final Result:**
**Lactic acid** is produced.

lessons.title: The Flow of Matter and Energy through Different Trophic Levels

cards.title: 3.3 The Flow of Matter and Energy through Different Trophic Levels
body: All living organisms need energy for various body activities such as growth, movement and reproduction.
All living organisms in an ecosystem need energy in order to stay alive.
All the energy in an ecosystem comes from the sun.
When a plant needs energy, it breaks down some of this food by respiration and energy is released.
Living organisms are classified as autotrophs and heterotrophs, based on how they obtain their food.

cards.title: The Flow of Matter and Energy through Different Trophic Levels
body: Energy and matter move through **trophic levels**: producer → primary consumer → secondary… About 10% of energy is passed on (school figure) — the rest is lost as heat, waste, unused bits. Food chain is one line; food web is many linked chains. Decomposers recycle matter back to the soil.

cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify functions of organelles**
*   Chloroplasts perform photosynthesis.
*   Ribosomes perform protein synthesis.
*   Nucleus houses the DNA.
*   Mitochondria carry out the aerobic respiration process to generate ATP.

**Final Result:**
**Mitochondria**.

tips.text: Biomolecules consist of carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids. They are mainly made up of three elements: carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.
Carbohydrates are important structurally and functionally to all living cells. These biomolecules make up the chief constituents of the food we eat every day.
These large molecules are broken down into simple molecules inside the cell with the help of different enzymes, which provide us with energy.
The released energy is used for various body processes.
Enzymes are proteins that act as catalysts, remaining unchanged by the reactions. They are critical molecules because they control basic life processes such as the synthesis of proteins and enzymes.
Where do animal cells get their energy from? 4.

Photosynthesis is a chemical process that takes place in plants to make food. It literally means synthesizing sugar molecules using light energy (“photo” means “light” and “synthesis” is to “assemble” or “produce”).
Green plants use solar energy to make biomolecules.
Most plants have a green substance, called chlorophyll, found inside the chloroplasts of plant cells.
Chlorophyll absorbs the light energy needed for photosynthesis.
Formula: Photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ Light + chlorophyll. Respiration is the reverse energy story: glucose broken to release ATP.
